A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Identity Bridge research. Their main text, equations, figures, references, and Appendices A and B are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original one-layer transformer experiments and Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct experiments on Husband-Wife and Parent-Child reversal tasks, including ablations and appendix diagnostics.

after.justification: v2 retains the original symbolic experiments and reports revised LLM experiments, three-seed evaluations, data-format and name-length ablations, and a new weight-decay study.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 substantially revises the practical training recipe from four-pattern OCR+ to three-pattern OCR-k. The composed forward example is retained and repeated k times, with k=6 in the main experiments; which entity receives a compositional identity example is reversed, and the plain forward example is omitted from the proposed recipe. The architecture, loss, and formal Identity Bridge construction remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same symbolic reversal task, Husband-Wife and Parent-Child tasks, and number/normal/long-name scenarios. Revised prompt formulations, repetition factors, and weight-decay settings change procedures within this coverage rather than introduce a new domain or task.

E2.justification: v2 adds an explicitly evaluated forward-only FWD comparator to the LLM comparisons in Figures 6 and 9; v1's corresponding main LLM figure shows only the proposed recipe across two tasks. Figure 7 also replaces the OCR/OCR+ comparison with revised OCR-1, OCR-3, and OCR-6 variants alongside IDN. The symbolic forward-only comparison is retained.

E3.justification: The LLM test prompt changes from asking the name of Bob's wife to asking directly for Bob's wife, and LLM MRR evaluation is removed. Appendix B changes the batch-size rule from one-fifth to one-tenth of the dataset, expands learning-rate search through 0.001, and replaces fixed weight decay 0.3 with a search. Plots extend to 2,500 steps, and name-length settings change from token-count ranges to specified 1/2/3-token categories.

E4.justification: Section 4.2.1 replaces the extra-prompt OCR+ ablation with a forward-example repetition study at k=1, 3, and 6, with revised shortcut probes. New Section 4.2.3 and Table 1 examine seven weight-decay settings. Name-length analysis is retained under revised settings, while Appendix B's first-token MRR diagnostic is removed.

E5.justification: v2 first reports three random seeds for each LLM experiment and introduces shaded bands throughout the LLM result plots; v1 supplies neither a run count nor comparable variability reporting. Appendix B explains that seed runs shuffle the dataset before training. The bands' statistical meaning remains undefined, and the PDFs do not establish an increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: The LLM results are substantially replaced: reported main accuracy changes from approximately 40% to 50%, and long-name accuracy from 7% to 10%, under different recipes and settings rather than a controlled performance comparison. v2 adds FWD results near zero, repetition-factor rankings, and Table 1's peak mean accuracy of 0.55 at weight decay 0.30. LLM MRR and first-token MRR results disappear; the symbolic results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Assumption 3.1, Lemma 3.2, Theorems 3.3 and 3.4, Proposition 3.5, and the Appendix A proofs are retained. The added discussion connecting weight decay to nuclear-norm bias cites prior work without introducing a new formal result or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statement, and conclusion raise the headline empirical claim from 40% to 50% reversal success. The central novelty claim, theoretical contribution, and claim of avoiding reversed training facts or architectural/loss changes retain their previous scope.

C2.justification: The empirical explanation shifts from an extra prompt suppressing copying shortcuts to competition between shortcut learning and reversal learning, with repeated forward facts providing the main learning signal. v2 adds a weight-decay interpretation through nuclear-norm bias and removes the earlier token-position MRR and low-confidence explanations. The broader shortcut and multi-token limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly documents disabling in-training shuffling to keep related examples together and shuffling before separate seed runs, alongside revised hyperparameter and batching information. The explicit temperature-40 disclosure in v1 disappears without a replacement value; this establishes a documentation removal, not a confirmed temperature change.

R1.justification: v2 adds Mikolov et al. (2013) to support the embedding analogy and Kobayashi et al. (2024) for the weight-decay interpretation. It removes Zhang et al. (2025), Training dynamics of in-context learning in linear attention, and the associated motivation about parameterization-dependent dynamics. The main related-work positioning is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in Section 4.2 and Appendix B, explaining the revised prompts, comparisons, and interpretations. Section 4.2.1 is retitled and Section 4.2.3 is added, with smaller introductory edits. The overall section organization and extensive theoretical exposition remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 6-8 are substantially redesigned with different comparison curves, shaded bands, revised legends and axes, and removed MRR panels. Figure 6 separates the two tasks into four panels. Appendix training-loss displays are reorganized into Figures 9-11, replacing the previous first-token MRR figure, and Table 1 is new. Figures 1-5 retain their underlying content with sizing and formatting adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical validation through explicit LLM forward-only controls, three-seed reporting, and analyses of repetition and weight decay. These provide a limited but clear quality gain beyond the higher headline accuracy. Undefined variability bands and incomplete hyperparameter disclosure still constrain reproducibility, while first-token diagnostics are lost. The 40%-to-50% change itself does not establish improvement because the training recipes and evaluation settings differ.
